synthesis: Scout's historical 15/30/60-day path layer has NO zoom floor and NO bounding-box restriction on its fetch, so the client pulls and renders every path point for the whole window (and, on Bird's Eye, every org kit) into one deck.gl PathLayer — the exploding payload that crashes the browser at 30/60 days. The fix mirrors patterns already proven in this exact codebase: the hit-icon markers already have a zoom floor (RANGE_HIT_MARKERS_MIN_ZOOM=12, render-only because that endpoint is row-capped), and the Direct/Staging order-density layers already bbox-fetch and re-query on pan/zoom (fetchOrdersHeatmap/fetchHitsHeatmap + onBoundsChanged idle + AbortController) — but the order layers have no zoom floor yet, so AC1's order-layer gating is a genuine additive gap. The real work: (1) give the path PathLayer AND the order GeoJsonLayer a zoom floor mirroring rangeHitMarkersEligible/syncRangeHitVisibility, gating the FETCH itself (not just render) since scan-paths has no server-side cap; (2) give scan-paths the same bbox-scoped, re-query-on-pan/zoom fetch the order layers already have. Driver-verified data-source split: the DRIVER historical path uses KitHistoricPositionsQuery over raw clarity.sc_positions (per-point rows → bbox is a plain lat/lng WHERE), while the ADMIN/Bird's Eye scanPaths uses KitScanPathsQuery over clarity.kit_scan_paths where path_points is Array(Tuple(Float64,Float64)) → bbox needs an array predicate (arrayExists) and fans across ALL org kits (the 'all kits + 30 days' crash trigger). So bbox must be added in TWO query classes with TWO techniques. A third non-obvious item: prefetchAllRangePaths (via usePrefetch.js) background-downloads the full un-bboxed 15/30/60-day payload ~2s after every mount on BOTH surfaces — it silently defeats AC3 unless reworked/removed. This is a FEATURE-route ticket with material, ticket-acknowledged design-approval decisions (zoom thresholds, snap-to-zoom-vs-fitToScanPaths, the admin array-bbox semantics, prefetch disposition, hit-density-layer symmetry, geohash-vs-raw-lines) that must NOT be auto-answered — gate is BLOCKED.

scope.summary: Add a zoom floor (client render + FETCH skip, mirroring RANGE_HIT_MARKERS_MIN_ZOOM/rangeHitMarkersEligible/syncRangeHitVisibility) to the historical scan-path PathLayer and the Direct/Staging order GeoJsonLayer; add bbox params + re-query-on-pan/zoom to the scan-path fetch (mirroring the already-bbox-aware fetchOrdersHeatmap flow) across BOTH backends — the driver KitHistoricPositionsQuery (raw sc_positions, simple lat/lng WHERE) and the admin/Bird's Eye KitScanPathsQuery (kit_scan_paths MV, path_points Array(Tuple), needs arrayExists); and rein in the unscoped background prefetch (usePrefetch.js -> prefetchAllRangePaths) so it can't reintroduce the crash. Both Scout surfaces share ScannerMap.vue/stores/map.js/ScoutHome.vue so one frontend change lands on both; the backend bbox work must be done twice with two techniques. Any bbox param added to the shared KitScanPathsQuery MUST be optional/additive (a non-Scout caller depends on it).

No zoom-snap exists today.

proposed_changes.change: Add validated OPTIONAL north/south/east/west (+ snapBbox) to scanPaths() (~39-112), threading the bbox into KitHistoricPositionsQuery on the historical (range) branch, mirroring how heatmapHits()/heatmapOrders() (~281-364) already validate+snap. proposed_changes.reason: Driver historical scan-paths has zero geographic scoping; its data source (raw sc_positions points) is trivially bbox-filterable with a WHERE.

proposed_changes.change: Add the same OPTIONAL bbox threading to the org-wide scanPaths() (~219-263), passed into KitScanPathsQuery. This is the endpoint behind the ticket's stated real-world trigger ('all kits + 30 days + search') — payload scales with days AND kit count with no per-kit or bbox cap.
proposed_changes.reason: Admin/Bird's Eye scanPaths fans KitScanPathsQuery across every scoped kit with no viewport restriction — the primary crash source.

proposed_changes.change: Add an OPTIONAL lat/lng bbox WHERE (tupleElement(geo,1)/(geo,2)) before decimation/grouping. Straightforward per-point filter; used by driver scanPaths() and livePath().
proposed_changes.reason: This is the driver historical path source (raw sc_positions rows) — a simple WHERE, the easy half of the two-technique bbox split. Candidate 1 missed this class by wrongly attributing the driver path to KitScanPathsQuery.

proposed_changes.change: Add an OPTIONAL/ADDITIVE bbox predicate against the path_points Array(Tuple(Float64,Float64)) column (e.g. arrayExists to keep buckets whose path touches the bbox). Predicate semantics + push-down-vs-PHP are pending question (c). MUST remain backward-compatible (bbox optional) — a non-Scout caller (KitUserPathController) shares this class.

Filter for render after segments are built, or expand the query bbox with margin.

questions.q: (a) ZOOM THRESHOLD: what zoom floor should the path AND order layers hide/fetch below — reuse RANGE_HIT_MARKERS_MIN_ZOOM=12, or a lower value? One shared const or per-layer/per-range?
questions.answer: Reuse zoom 12 as a single SHARED const (e.g. PATH_LAYERS_MIN_ZOOM=12) for the path + order (+ hit-density, per (e)) gating — consistent with the existing hit-icon RANGE_HIT_MARKERS_MIN_ZOOM=12; tune later if needed. Not per-range.

YES snap-to-zoom: selecting 15/30/60 snaps the map to the gate zoom (>=12) so the layer is immediately visible, AND DROP the current fitToScanPaths() zoom-OUT behavior (it fights the gate and assumes the whole path set is in memory, which conflicts with bbox-scoped fetching). Snap-to-zoom is now IN scope (DateRangeControl.vue selectRange wiring is no longer contingent).

questions.q: (c) ADMIN BBOX SEMANTICS for KitScanPathsQuery over path_points Array(Tuple).
questions.answer: arrayExists any-point-in-bbox, PUSHED DOWN into ClickHouse (a bucket is 'in view' if ANY of its points falls in the bbox). No MV/query restructure to point-level storage — that stays a potential follow-up, out of scope here.

DROP the long-range (15/30/60) background prefetch entirely — do not rework it to viewport-scoped. On-demand bbox-scoped fetch replaces it. (A shorter/today prefetch that is small may remain, but the exploding long ranges must not be background-pulled.)

notes: RESOLVED DESIGN DECISIONS (Dalton, 2026-07-14) — the plan MUST follow these: (a) ONE shared zoom floor = 12 (new const, mirror RANGE_HIT_MARKERS_MIN_ZOOM) for path + order + hit-density layers, gating FETCH and render; (b) selecting 15/30/60 SNAPS the map to zoom>=12 and the fitToScanPaths() zoom-OUT is DROPPED/neutralized; (c) admin KitScanPathsQuery bbox = arrayExists any-point-in-bbox pushed down in ClickHouse (no MV restructure); (d) DROP the long-range (15/30/60) background prefetch entirely (prefetchAllRangePaths/usePrefetch.js); (e) ALSO zoom-gate the Direct Hit Density circle layer (HitDirectHotspotQuery/'hits'); (f) geohash heatmap DEFERRED (not this pass). bbox params on KitScanPathsQuery stay OPTIONAL/additive (KitUserPathController backward-compat).

The hit-icon zoom gate (RANGE_HIT_MARKERS_MIN_ZOOM=12 + rangeHitMarkersEligible()/syncRangeHitVisibility(), local consts in ScannerMap.vue) is RENDER-ONLY: its /map/hits endpoint is row-capped at MAX_MAP_HITS=100, so fetch cost is bounded. Scan-paths has NO such cap — the new path/order gating MUST also skip the FETCH below the floor, or AC3 (no crash) is not satisfied. [settled across all 3 candidates]

The Direct/Staging order-density layers ALREADY bbox-fetch and re-query on pan/zoom (fetchOrdersHeatmap/fetchHitsHeatmap + onBoundsChanged idle listener, 300ms debounce, per-layer AbortController; server snapBbox 0.02deg grid, client VIEW_SNAP_STEP=0.02) — confirming the ticket's premise — but have NO zoom floor, so AC1's order-layer gating is a real additive gap. [settled]

fitToScanPaths() (ScannerMap.vue ~1413-1445) zooms OUT to fit all fetched paths on entering Historical — directly conflicts with the 'snap to a zoom level' fuller vision and assumes the full path set is in memory (incompatible with bbox-scoped fetch). Tied to question (b). [settled]

DATA-SOURCE SPLIT (driver-verified, corrects candidate 1): driver historical 15/30/60 path uses KitHistoricPositionsQuery over raw clarity.sc_positions (per-point rows → simple lat/lng WHERE); driver 'today' uses KitScanPathsQuery(layer 'today'); admin/Bird's Eye scanPaths uses KitScanPathsQuery over clarity.kit_scan_paths where path_points is Array(Tuple(Float64,Float64)) → needs an array predicate (arrayExists) and fans across ALL org kits (the 'all kits + 30 days' crash trigger). bbox must be added in TWO query classes with TWO techniques.

The driver-side bbox filter interacts with HistoricPathBuilder::build() segment-break logic (app/Support/Scout/HistoricPathBuilder.php:52-80): it compares each point to the immediately preceding one to decide line breaks, so filtering points before segmentation can create spurious breaks/joins at the viewport edge. Filter for render after segments are built, or expand the query bbox with a margin. [grounded, not a blocker]

grounding.code_flow: DateRangeControl.vue selectRange() -> dashboard.setRange() -> ScoutHome.vue watch(dashboard.range) -> mapStore.setRange + mapStore.fetchScanPaths(range) [no bounds] -> GET /map/scan-paths?range=X -> (driver) ClarityScoutMapController::scanPaths -> KitHistoricPositionsQuery (raw sc_positions, single kit) -> HistoricPathBuilder::build -> full per-hour path array; (admin) ClarityScoutBirdsEyeController::scanPaths -> KitScanPathsQuery (kit_scan_paths MV, path_points array, ALL org kits) -> full unbounded return -> mapStore.scanPaths -> ScannerMap.vue updateOverlayLayers() pushes ALL of it into one unconditional PathLayer -> browser OOMs at 30/60d. data_impact.mv_or_cdc_implications: clarity.kit_scan_paths is a ReplacingMergeTree MV (TTL 90d, read with FINAL, <=15-min cadence) storing one path_points Array(Tuple(Float64,Float64)) per kit/bucket — a bbox predicate needs an array function (arrayExists/arrayFilter), not a plain WHERE; query-logic-only, no migration. clarity.sc_positions (KitHistoricPositionsQuery) is per-point rows → trivial lat/lng WHERE, no MV/CDC implication. The bbox predicate cannot use the ORDER BY (org_id,kit_id,timestamp) key, so ClickHouse still scans the org/kit/time partition and filters bbox post-scan — this doesn't cut CH-side cost much but dramatically cuts the HTTP payload, consistent with the ticket's framing that CH already handles the query fine and the win is in what's returned/rendered.
